newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, having added reserves on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
But sometime between now and after the Thanksgiving Day holiday, the Fed will need to add permanent reserves to the banking system by buying coupons outright, they said.

Fed funds traded at 5-1/8 percent in late morning, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate, indicating that the three-day system operation the Fed conducted on Monday had added enough reserves to the banking system, analysts said.
"Yesterday's three-day system repo should keep the Fed on the sidelines today," analysts at UBS Securities said in a joint release.
Analysts at MMS International also said they expected the Fed to stay out of the market.
"Fed funds are on the soft side and should remain so most of the day," they observed.
Analysts said the Fed must soon add permanent reserves to the banking system buy buying coupons.
"We see the possibility of a coupon pass as soon as today," said the MMS analysts.

Economists at UBS Securities said that with currency in circulation typically rising around the Thanksgiving holiday, "it remains likely that the Fed will buy coupon securities outright starting Thursday.
"If the Fed does not initiate the coupon pass this week, it will likely wait until after Thanksgiving, during the first week of December, to buy securities," they said.
-- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679
